title: Man. Post. Cap. II Status Questionis: poenae nomen ambiguous — hereditary corruption as penalty?
pass_a_gloss: CHAPTER II. Status of the question. I come now to the status of the question. You would not have set it awkwardly if to the name of penalty, which you introduced into it, you had either not included ambiguity, or had removed it. For truly, by the name of penalty you either wished to embrace hereditary corruption, or you did not wish to. If you did not wish to: you ought to have signified that, otherwise to the reader about to err, inasmuch as in this first chapter you hint, and in the second you cry out, and to others you inculcate, that that corruption is the penalty of the first sin. If you wished, or thought, that that corruption is the penalty properly so called of the first sin, not only inasmuch as it was in Adam himself, but also inasmuch as it is in us; or not. If the former, I do not admit the question: For it presupposes as certain, as confessed among us, that which I refuted by my theses, and which is at issue in the question, namely that hereditary corruption is, properly and strictly speaking, the penalty of the first sin, not only inasmuch as it was in Adam but also inasmuch as it is present propagated to us. If indeed you wished it to be a penalty, but not properly so called, nor in the strict signification of this word, at least inasmuch as it is in us, it was fitting that you explain your mind, since it appears from many places of this your treatise that you think that corruption to be a penalty in the strictest sense, and most properly.
pass_b_english: Chapter II. The state of the question. I come now to the state of the question. You would not have framed it awkwardly if, in the word penalty that you brought into it, you had either left out the ambiguity or taken it away. For by penalty you either meant to include hereditary corruption, or you did not. If you did not, you should have said so—otherwise the reader will go wrong—since in this first chapter you hint, in the second you cry out, and elsewhere you drum into others, that that corruption is the penalty of the first sin. If you meant, or thought, that that corruption is the first sin's penalty in the proper sense, not only as it was in Adam himself but also as it is in us—or not—then, if the former, I refuse the question. It assumes as settled among us what I refuted in my theses and what is still under dispute: that hereditary corruption is, properly and strictly, the penalty of the first sin not only as it was in Adam but also as it is present in us by propagation. If you meant a penalty, but not properly so called, nor in the strict sense of the word—at least as it is in us—you ought to have explained your mind; for from many places in this treatise of yours it is plain that you take that corruption to be a penalty in the strictest and most proper sense.
source_text: CAP. II. Status Questionis. Venio nunc ad statum questionis. Eum non incommode constituisses si poenae nomini, quod in eam introduxisti, ambiguitatem vel non inclusisses, vel sustulisses. Enimvero poenae nomine corruptionem haereditariam complecti vel voluisti, vel noluisti. Si noluisti: debuisti id significare, alioqui erraturo lectori, quippe cum hoc primo capite innuas, et secundo clames, et aliis inculces, corruptionem illam poenam esse primi peccati. Si voluisti, vel putasti corruptionem illam esse poenam proprie dictam primi peccati, non solum quatenus in ipso Adamo fuit, sed etiam quatenus inest in nobis; vel non. Si prius, quaestionem non admitto: Praesupponit enim ut certum, ut inter nos confessum, id quod ego thesibus meis refutavi, quodque versatur in quaestione, nimirum corruptionem haereditariam esse, proprie et stricte loquendo, poenam primi peccati, non solum quatenus fuit in Adamo sed etiam quatenus nobis propagata inest. Si poenam quidem esse voluisti, sed non proprie dictam, nec stricta hujus vocabuli significatione, saltem quatenus est in nobis, decuit te mentem tuam explicare, quoniam apparet ex multis hujus tui tractatus locis te corruptionem illam putare poenam esse sensu strictissimo, maximeque proprio.

choices.choice: Refuse question if hereditary corruption assumed as proper penalty of first sin in us
choices.why: Cap. II open clears Garissoles's status
